source.document_reference: APQC PCF Cross-Industry v8.0 (Feb 2026), 9.6.1 Process accounts payable (10756); step decomposition per PhD encoding spec v1.0 with HighRadius/Trintech/KnowledgeLeader practitioner documentation. APQC activity IDs pending verification against PCF v8.0 text.

steps.name: Match dataset assembly
steps.description: The invoice under test is paired with its purchase order and goods receipt note, retrieved from the ERP, forming the complete document set on which the match is executed.

steps.name: Quantity matching
steps.description: Invoiced quantities are compared line by line against quantities received per the goods receipt note, producing per-line quantity variances.

steps.name: Price and terms matching
steps.description: Invoiced unit prices, discounts and tax treatment are compared line by line against the purchase order, producing per-line price and terms variances.

steps.name: Tolerance evaluation
steps.description: Quantity and price variances are evaluated against the organisation's tolerance policy, classifying the match as clean, within tolerance, or an exception requiring investigation.

steps.name: Exception investigation and resolution
steps.description: Matches classified as exceptions are investigated against source documents and vendor correspondence, and resolved as accepted, corrected or rejected, with the resolution evidenced.

steps.name: Match release approval
steps.description: Cleanly matched, tolerance-passed and exception-resolved invoices are reviewed and released for posting and payment processing, with releases outside standard tolerance requiring explicit approval.

steps.name: Match control reporting
steps.description: Match outcomes, tolerance overrides and exception resolutions are logged to the control record, and periodic match-rate and override reporting is produced for control review.

requirements.statement: Quantity matching against goods receipt data must survive the redesign in some form.
Price and terms matching against purchase order data must survive the redesign in some form.
Whatever carries the quantity matching function must still consume goods receipt note data.
Whatever carries the price and terms matching function must still consume purchase order data.
Tolerance evaluation against a stated tolerance policy must survive in some form; matching without a tolerance discipline is not a control.
Whatever carries the tolerance evaluation function must still consume the tolerance policy.
Match release approval must survive in some form.
Exception resolution must occur before match release approval.
The exception resolution function and the release approval function must not be performed by the same actor.
